# DiAlgo

> DiAlgo (dialgo.net) is a mobile app for iPhone and Android that connects an older or dependent person with their family: the person taps one of a few large buttons ("Good morning", "I'm fine", "Call me", "I need help") and the message reaches the whole family, who also share medication reminders and medical appointments. It is published by ArnoHealth S.L. (onmedic), Barcelona, Spain. It is not related to the domain dialgo.com.

Canonical site: https://dialgo.net/
Last updated: 2026-10-31
Publisher: ArnoHealth S.L. (onmedic, https://onmedic.com/), founded by Albert Arnó (https://albertarno.net/about/)
Languages: Spanish (default, `/`), Catalan (`/ca/`) and English (`/en/`). The app is available in the same three languages.

## App availability and price

- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/es/app/dialgo/id6738914468)
- [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.arnohealth.dialgo)
- 14-day free trial with no card, then EUR 6.99 per month in Spain (the price may vary by country and store). Only the family administrator pays; there is no limit on family members. Store listing texts may still show older figures until the next app release; this site is current.

## What DiAlgo is not

- It is not a medical device and does not provide medical advice, diagnosis or treatment.
- It is not telecare or an emergency service: the "I need help" button alerts the family, not the emergency services. It does not locate the person or detect falls.
- No clinical study has measured the effect of DiAlgo itself. The research cited on the site supports design decisions, not outcome claims.
